articles.title: Ukraine Air Raid App Hacked to Send Fake Nuclear Warnings
articles.description: Ukraine's air raid alert app was hacked to send fake radiation warnings in Kyiv. This occurred after a ceasefire in Kherson ended. Officials confirmed the hack and urge calm.

articles.title: Russia Launches Ballistic Missile on Kyiv Amidst Cyber Attacks and Protest Waves
articles.description: Russia has launched a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv hours after President Zelenskyy warned of a major strike, while cyber actors targeting messaging apps compromise emergency alert systems that falsely warned of nuclear and chemical attacks. Concurrently, France deploys 70,000 police officers for Halloween protests, and Albania sees lawmakers disrupt parliament during ongoing civil unrest.

articles.title: Ukraines Air Raid Alerts Hacked With Fake Radiation Warnings; Russia Reports Cyberattack On Emergency App
articles.description: Ukraine reports hacked air raid alerts carrying fake chemical and radiation warnings, while Russia says its emergency app was targeted in a major cyberattack spreading false public safety information.

articles.title: Nuclear War Scare grips Russia, Ukraine as Hackers push Fake Emergency Alerts
articles.description: MOSCOW – Fake nuclear attack warnings triggered alarm as Russia and Ukraine report massive cyberattacks on their emergency alert systems. Hackers spread terrifying messages about nuclear-armed drones as ceasefire expired, raising fears of renewed fighting and escalating cyberwarfare. articles.title: 'Radiation warning, public threat': Russia, Ukraine suffer massive cyberattacks on emergency alert systems
articles.description: Ukraine and Russia both reported cyberattacks on their emergency alert systems on Nov 2, which triggered fake warnings of chemical and radiation threats in Ukraine and altered public safety alerts via a Russian government app. Meanwhile, President Zelensky called for an energy ceasefire

articles.title: Six days of respite in Oleshky end as Russia and Ukraine target critical infrastructure
articles.description: A six-day humanitarian ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky has come to an end, closing a rare window for aid deliveries and civilian evacuations. Meanwhile, cyberattacks have disrupted public warning apps in both countries, while drone strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure continue to fuel tensions
